title: TS SDK: Bridge patterns for ReadableStream <-> AsyncIterator, resumable retries, and backpressure
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Provide a set of TypeScript SDK patterns and concrete helpers that make it ergonomic to consume and expose streaming responses as either Web ReadableStreams (Web Streams API) or AsyncIterators, with robust retry/resume semantics and clear backpressure/cancellation behavior. Motivation: customers build both browser and Node integrations and expect first-class interop between async iteration and Web Streams. We have recurring support bugs and subtle developer mistakes around cancellation, lost events on reconnect, and double-consume errors.

Scope: deliver API helpers, three canonical wrapper implementations, comprehensive tests (unit + e2e with local mock server), documentation/examples, and a lightweight strategy pattern for configurable retry/resume behavior. We will not change underlying runtime kernel selection or network protocols in this ticket; that is covered by ENG-59812.

Design constraints and principles:
- Single-consume safety: wrappers should throw early when double-consume is attempted and provide a clear migration guide.
- Explicit cancellation token support across both APIs.
- Backpressure semantics must align with platform expectations: Node streams and Web Streams should exert pull-based backpressure while async iterators should allow consumer-driven pace.
- Retry/resume should be opt-in and checkpoint-aware: resumability requires server-side support for offsets or user-provided checkpoints; fallback policy should avoid duplicate delivery when possible.
- Minimal runtime footprint: helpers should be zero-deps and tree-shakeable for browser bundles.

Deliverables:
1) streamHelpers.ts: utility functions for conversions and cancellation propagation.
2) streaming-client adapter: a factory that exposes three APIs from the same underlying transport: asAsyncIterator(), asReadableStream(), asDualConsumeWrapper().
3) Retry strategies: simple (no-resume, full-retry), resume-by-checkpoint (when server returns resume token), and idempotent-window (best-effort dedupe).
4) Example app: small browser + Node example showing how to switch between APIs without changing business logic.
5) Docs: Console docs + code snippets + migration guide from older SDK streams.

Notes on compatibility: Node 18+ and modern browsers. We'll use native ReadableStream types and AsyncGenerator syntax in TS declarations.
acceptance_criteria: Library exposes stable helpers in @redwood/sdk: streamToAsyncIterator, asyncIteratorToReadableStream, createStreamingClientFactory
Helpers preserve cancellation: abort signals passed to the factory are wired to underlying transport and downstream consumers
Retry/resume strategies are configurable; resume-by-checkpoint successfully replays from server resume token in integration test
Comprehensive tests cover: double-consume detection, cancellation propagation, backpressure under slow consumer, and retry window semantics
Examples for browser and Node are published in docs and linked from README

comments: 2025-01-10 Asha Patel: Created ticket after several customer reports where browser apps lost streaming events when reconnecting. Initial goals set; flagged dependency on ENG-59812 for transport retry hooks.

2025-01-15 Miguel Santos: Drafted API signatures. Posting here for early feedback: streamToAsyncIterator(readable: ReadableStream, options?) and asyncIteratorToReadableStream(iterable: AsyncIterable, options?). Also proposing createStreamingClientFactory(transport, opts) that returns { asAsyncIterator, asReadableStream, asDualConsume }.

2025-01-18 Lina Zhou (reviews): Concern: dual-consume wrapper could encourage bad patterns. Suggest split into explicit 'single-owner' wrapper that enforces one consume path, and a 'proxy' that supports both but with clear runtime checks.

2025-01-22 Miguel Santos: Implemented MVP and pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123 — includes streamHelpers and basic adapters. Unit tests included. Requesting review from @lina and @ashap.

2025-01-24 Lina Zhou: Reviewed PR; requested additional tests around AbortSignal crossing from ReadableStream cancel() to underlying transport. Also flagged a race where resume token is dropped if transport fails before header propagation. Added comment on PR.

2025-01-30 Miguel Santos: Addressed review comments, added test harness for resume token propagation, and added documentation draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/streaming-interop (confluence mirror: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Streaming+Interop+Patterns)

2025-02-03 QA-Bot: Ran canary in internal staging for 48h. Observed one failure where slow consumer + aggressive retry resulted in duplicated first 2 events. Root cause: resume token TTL shorter than client retry window. Added follow-up task to coordinate with transport team (ENG-60234).
